title: Affine chart test for a fibre after arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ and $g:T'\to T$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], put $X'=X\times_TT'$ and $f':X'\to T'$ [def-pc-base-change], and choose $t'\in T'$ with $t=g(t')$. Set $k=\kappa(t)$ and $L=\kappa(t')$, with the residue-field embedding $k\to L$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $Y=X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be any affine open cover, with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ as $k$-schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $H/L$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Give $H$ its composite $k$-algebra structure. There is a canonical isomorphism $Z_H:=X'\times_{T'}\operatorname{Spec}H\cong Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}H$ compatible with the maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}H$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The inverse images of the $U_i$ under $Z_H\to Y$ form an affine open cover of $Z_H$ and are canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kH)$, with their projections given by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $h\mapsto1\otimes h$. Consequently $Z_H$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] if and only if every $A_i\otimes_kH$ is reduced, meaning it has no nonzero nilpotent element. Tensor products have multiplication $(a\otimes h)(b\otimes j)=ab\otimes hj$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is no finiteness, flatness or nonemptiness hypothesis; $I=\varnothing$ is allowed when $Y$ is empty.

proof.text: Let b:Spec H→Spec κ(g(t′)) be the given composite algebra map, d:Spec H→T′ the given map, q:Z_H→Spec H its second projection and x:Z_H→X the composite first projection. Naturality of fromSpecResidueField and hH give d≫g=b≫fromSpecResidueField. The pullback identities give x≫f=(q≫b)≫fromSpecResidueField. Define p by the universal property of the fibre pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections x and q≫b. Pasting the square defining Z_H with X×_T T′ gives the outer cartesian square over T. Cancelling the cartesian square defining the fibre, using [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], shows that (p,q) is cartesian over Spec κ(g(t′)). Its universal comparison isomorphism e has the asserted projection identities.

source.place: Tag 0576, lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced, fibre identity expanded by two pullback pastings

proof.text: The first projection W_i:=Z_H×_Y Spec A_i→Z_H is an open immersion by base change of the given open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. Pasting its defining cartesian square with (p,q), and using hι, gives a cartesian square W_i→Spec A_i over Spec H→Spec κ(g(t′)). Its comparison isomorphism followed by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives c_i:W_i≅Spec(A_i⊗_k H). The projection formulas follow from isoPullback_inv_fst/snd and pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst/snd. The tensor algebra is Mathlib’s standard commutative algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) and 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), including the projection-compatible tensor construction

proof.text: Given z∈Z_H, choose a∈Spec A_i over p(z) using the original cover. Surjectivity of the scheme pullback comparison on underlying points (Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback, the pointwise consequence of [def-pc-fibre-product]) produces w∈W_i over z. Hence these open immersions form an open cover. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-open-cover]. Reducedness transfers in both directions across c_i via isReduced_of_isOpenImmersion [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff] then gives precisely reducedness of A_i⊗_k H. The pointwise cover construction and universal quantification need no inhabited-index or nonempty-chart hypothesis, so also prove the empty cases.
